name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:mocks → /spec:plan → /spec:run (build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:fix. Changelog (last 3): 7.286.0 — Decision-lint now reads three structural triggers when a spec locks. A spec with breaking: true needs a [breaking:] or [asked:] tag on a Decision, or it fails as breaking-unasked. A File Plan row that touches a dependency file prints an advisory notice and must name the packages, or it fails as missing-dependency-names. A non-empty Data Model must be tier critical and carry an existing rows: line. The File Plan parser gains a Summary column, and release Phase 0 now lists breaking specs under a warning-sign breaking heading. 7.285.0 — four owner questions where a silent default cannot be undone: /spec:release asks before rolling back a failed production check (release.rollbackCommand, rollback leg on the release row); /spec:plan confirms a critical-tier lock; review's MERGE step counts a prototype's unmerged commits and asks before deleting them (--prototype delete|keep); new secrets-scan.js behind spec-paths secrets-scan. 7.284.0 — Session token usage on ledger rows: build and review rows carry sessionTokens as their last key — the orchestrating session's own transcript usage during the stage (input, cacheCreate, cacheRead, output counters and turns) as a delta between sidecar creation and row write, deduplicated by message id because the transcript repeats a message's usage on every content-block line; null when the stamp or transcript is absent or the stamp moved mid-stage. lib/session-stamp.js gains sessionUsage(root) and usageDelta(); verdict.js gains --sessionTokens <json> (review profile only, refused on release, absent flag adds no key). Subagent spend is not included; the name says so. Motivated by the 2026-10-29 model-placement review: nothing measured what a seat change costs.
